topics.question: Why does multiplying by a fraction sometimes make a number smaller?
topics.coverage: Use area models and scaling to distinguish multiplication from repeated whole-number addition.

topics.question: What makes a mathematical proof different from checking many examples?
topics.coverage: Contrast finite tests, universal statements and a counterexample using an accessible divisibility claim.

topics.question: Why do negative numbers obey a consistent multiplication rule?
topics.coverage: Compare number-line patterns and distributive reasoning; separate a motivating model from a formal definition.

topics.question: What does a function describe beyond a formula on a graph?
topics.coverage: Connect inputs, outputs, domain and multiple representations with a piecewise real-world example.

topics.question: How can the same area fit inside shapes with different perimeters?
topics.coverage: Compare rectangles and curved boundaries; distinguish exact results from a numerical search.

topics.question: Why does a derivative describe change at a single point?
topics.coverage: Build from average rates and shrinking intervals; state where corners or discontinuities break the simple picture.

topics.question: How does an integral add quantities when their rate keeps changing?
topics.coverage: Use distance from velocity and signed area; distinguish exact integration from numerical approximation.

topics.question: What does a matrix transformation do to an entire plane?
topics.coverage: Track basis vectors, area and composition; keep coordinate conventions explicit.

topics.question: What prevalence and error rates produce a nine-percent positive predictive value?
topics.coverage: Work an explicit 2-by-2 test table with stated sensitivity, specificity and base rate; show that '99% accurate' alone cannot determine the posterior. Medical interpretation belongs to a specialist review.

topics.question: Why can a problem be easy to check but difficult to solve?
topics.coverage: Introduce decision problems, certificates and scaling with a small combinatorial example; do not imply unresolved complexity questions are settled.

topics.question: How can infinity come in different sizes?
topics.coverage: Use one-to-one matching and a diagonal argument; distinguish mathematical cardinality from physical quantities.

topics.question: What makes a geometry possible without Euclid's parallel postulate?
topics.coverage: Compare local rules and triangle behavior on selected models; avoid equating curved surfaces with every non-Euclidean theory.

topics.question: How can a numerical method converge to the wrong-looking answer?
topics.coverage: Examine conditioning, finite precision and stopping criteria in a bounded root-finding problem.

topics.question: Why can a mathematical model be correct internally but unsuitable for its intended use?
topics.coverage: Separate assumptions, deduction, calibration and external validation using one population or transport model.

topics.question: Why is the zeta-regularized value of 1+2+3+... different from its ordinary sum?
topics.coverage: Define ordinary partial sums and analytic continuation separately; derive the domain and notation used for -1/12 without claiming a finite ordinary total.

topics.question: How does a differential equation express assumptions about the growth of a population?
topics.coverage: Compare exponential and resource-limited models, parameters, initial conditions, units and data mismatch; keep biological conclusions bounded by the model.

topics.question: Why can the shortest route for one vehicle fail to be the best routing plan for a whole fleet?
topics.coverage: Model vertices, edges, capacities, time windows and objectives in a small graph; separate a shortest-path problem from constrained multi-vehicle optimization.

topics.question: How does adding a constraint change an optimization problem's feasible solutions?
topics.coverage: Use a labeled production or scheduling example to compare objective, feasible region, binding constraints and sensitivity; distinguish mathematical optimum from a complete real-world decision.

categories.title: Notation as an enabling mathematical tool

topics.question: How can a change in notation make an existing mathematical idea easier to extend?
topics.coverage: Compare a bounded before-and-after example in algebra, calculus or vectors; separate a new representation from a claim of discovering the underlying relationship.

topics.question: What do surviving Ramanujan notebooks document, and what is later biography?
topics.coverage: Select a dated notebook entry and archival catalogue; separate mathematical formula and manuscript provenance from reported inspiration or a film's dramatization.

# Mathematics Channel Master Topic Roadmap (Scratch to Advanced)
**Niche:** 119 Mathematics (Math_Scientific_Methods)  
**Channel Language:** English (YouTube)  
**Target Audience:** Mathematicians, Computer Scientists, Logic Puzzle Enthusiasts, STEM Students, Number Theory Fans (Global)  
**Production Format:** 10-Minute Documentary Explainer Episodes (600s, 75 Fixed 8s Scenes)

## 1. Channel Progression Strategy

This curriculum organizes the core disciplines of Mathematics across four progressive tiers:
- **Tier 1: Number Theory, Geometry & Fundamental Constants (Beginner / Scratch)** — Prime numbers and the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, Euclidean geometry axiomatic method, irrationality of sqrt(2) and Pi, Euler's identity, and mathematical induction.
- **Tier 2: Calculus, Linear Algebra & Probability Distributions (Intermediate)** — Leibniz-Newton fundamental theorem of calculus, matrix transformations and eigenvalues/eigenvectors, Bayes' theorem probability calculus, and infinite series convergence/divergence.
- **Tier 3: Abstract Algebra, Topology & Incompleteness Theorems (Upper Intermediate)** — Group theory and Galois symmetry (unsolvability of the quintic), topological homeomorphisms (coffee cup vs donut), Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems, and non-Euclidean hyperbolic geometry.
- **Tier 4: The Millennium Prize Problems, Complex Analysis & The Master Equation (Advanced / Masterclass)** — The Riemann Hypothesis and prime distribution zeros, P vs NP computational complexity, Navier-Stokes smooth solutions, Hodge Conjecture, and the unreasonable effectiveness of math in physics.

prior_initial_map.name: Mathematics
prior_initial_map.purpose: A starting subject map for a Mathematics YouTube channel. Categories organize concrete subtopics; each entry supplies an episode question, a research outline and a boundary for case selection. Counts follow the authored coverage, with no imposed topic maximum.

Explain the proposed mechanism with an observable example; distinguish model from direct observation.

science.requirements: Use original observations or experiments, an appropriate scientific reference and the actual measurement method. Distinguish mechanisms, correlations, model assumptions, uncertainty and limits of generalization.
source_leads: methods papers and current scientific reference works

synthesis.requirements: Define the rival claims and their evidence standards. Compare sources on equal terms, separate empirical findings from values or interpretations and do not imply that all positions have equal evidential support.
source_leads: the original sources behind the compared claims

handoff: Keep the BANK ID in notes. Refine the research question with an exact text edition, jurisdiction, population, product version, place, time range or clearly labeled fictional premise.
Inspect actual sources; no source was verified by generating this map. Apply the existing registry planning and idea readiness process before project creation.
Choose a current registered angle only after reading its niche-specific scope. This initial map has not checked or assigned angle plans for these entries.
Keep Q1-Q42, CAT defaults, project snapshots, output locations and production gates unchanged. Catalog counts are not production or publication counts.
Review neighboring banks for semantic overlap and follow the existing Phase 1 claim-ledger requirements. Add qualified review when required by the production contract.
prior_initial_map.coverage_limits: This initial map does not exhaust the niche, its regions, time periods, named case studies, texts, technical variants or disputed questions. It has not performed source-feasibility checks, semantic duplicate review of every pair, trend analysis, claim verification or episode production. Expand any category freely after identifying a real coverage gap; add categories where the subject requires them. Preserve existing IDs when refining wording and allocate new IDs only for genuinely new proposals.

open_coverage.next_step: Clay Mathematics Institute pages establish current unsolved status and formal question boundaries for P vs NP and Riemann; see RESEARCH_NOTES/BANK-119-026.md. Archived Bitcoin, Ramanujan, Godel and infinite-sum hooks still need separate proof, history or application research. No idea or episode was approved.
